analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/provider/cli-reference.md, so no executable code, keys, authorization logic or protocol behavior changes. The visible patch excerpt adds (a) a note that shutdown waits up to 15 seconds per model unload and leaves a model whose native retirement never finishes to process exit (`ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown`), and (b) a status description of a restart-needed notice driven by `enabled_models_at_start` and `enabled_models_at_last_switch` in the daemon state. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the supplied base and head text units do not cover the changed line ranges (1210-1212, 1290-1305). I could not verify the rest of the documentation edits.

Threat-model relevance: the 15-second unload timeout touches T-028 (residual GPU/KV data) and T-010 (resource release). A model that never retires is left to process exit, so residual plaintext GPU memory persists until the process exits. This is only a documented shutdown bound. The underlying code change, if any, is outside the supplied evidence. Integration should check that the unload timeout does not skip KV/cache purge or the drain's usage-settlement guarantees. The new daemon-state fields are only model-ID lists and do not touch the A-001 or A-008 sensitive assets.

I examined the supplied base units (provider.toml keys, env passthrough, the SSD cache, App Attest worker, add-on sections) and head unit lines 1-385. They show no new endpoints, credential handling or cache-storage changes, and the T-041 cache posture claims are unchanged.
